title: Maintenance of Obstetric Registers and Records
path: Maintenance of Obstetric Registers and Records

headings.title: Introduction to Midwifery Documentation
headings.content: Midwifery documentation forms the backbone of safe clinical practice in Nigerian healthcare facilities. Every entry in a client file tells a story of care given, decisions made, and clinical findings observed. Accurate records provide a permanent legal account that protects both the mother and the midwife. When documentation is thorough, healthcare teams communicate seamlessly across different shifts. Without these records, continuity of care breaks down, putting vulnerable women and newborns at risk during labour and the postpartum period.

headings.title: Types of Maternity Registers
headings.content:
A maternity unit relies on several specialized registers to capture every phase of reproductive health. These bound books organize large volumes of data chronologically for public health tracking and internal audits.

- **Antenatal Register**: Captures booking details, gestational age, parity, and scheduled visit outcomes for pregnant women.
- **Labour Ward Register**: Records admission time, progress of cervical dilation, delivery route, birth weight, and immediate Apgar scores.
- **Postnatal Register**: Tracks maternal recovery, lochia checks, infant feeding establishment, and discharge dates.
- **Family Planning Register**: Documents client choices, contraceptive methods dispensed, and follow-up return dates.

headings.title: Best Practices for Making Entries
headings.content:
Writing in an official obstetric register requires discipline, legibility, and precision. Midwives must enter data immediately after performing a procedure or assessment to avoid memory lapses. 

1. **Timeliness**: Document events as they happen rather than waiting until the end of a busy shift.
2. **Legibility**: Write clearly so other professionals can read medication dosages and vital signs without guessing.
3. **Ink Standards**: Use permanent blue or black ink; never use pencils or erasable markers.
4. **Correction Method**: Draw a single clean line through an error, write the correct word above it, and sign or initial the correction next to it.

headings.title: Legal, Ethical, and Professional Accountability
headings.content: Obstetric records are legal documents admissible in courts of law. In a malpractice lawsuit or professional negligence inquiry, the client chart serves as primary evidence of whether standard care was delivered. Midwives carry personal professional accountability for every word they write or fail to write. Omitting a vital sign check is legally interpreted as a task undone. Maintaining professional integrity means records must never be backdated, falsified, or altered to hide a clinical error.

headings.title: Confidentiality, Security, and Storage
headings.content: Patient privacy is a fundamental human right and a core ethical duty in midwifery. Obstetric records contain intimate personal details that must be safeguarded against unauthorized access. Registers should never be left open on desks where visitors or uninvolved staff can view them. Physical records need secure storage in locked cabinets within restricted-access record rooms. When digital systems are used, password protection and secure logouts prevent breaches of confidential maternal health data.

headings.title: Auditing and Statistical Reporting
headings.content: Data extracted from maternity registers drive local and national health planning. Facility managers use these numbers to track maternal mortality rates, caesarean section frequencies, and antenatal attendance trends. Regular clinical audits compare actual documentation practices against established hospital guidelines to highlight areas needing staff training or resource allocation. Accurate tallying in daily registers ensures that government health ministries receive reliable statistics for policy making.
